notes.filename: Exploring Trade-Offs for Online Mental Health Matching- Agent-Based Modeling Study.md
verified: Status-quo rule is accurately stated: counselors choose randomly from the available seeker queue, with choice-time modeled exponentially at λ=1.25 (Methods, PDF p.6).

Alternative policies use applicant-proposing deferred acceptance; counselors accept the policy recommendation with probability 0.90 and make a random choice with probability 0.10. The seven named policies are correct (PDF pp.8-10).

Predictor summary is accurate: random forests use gender, birth year, and topic; rating prediction reports 0.72 accuracy/F1 with 80/20 split and SMOTE-balanced training, while blocking prediction reports 0.91 accuracy/F1 with an 80/20 split (PDF pp.7-8).
Validation reports Pearson correlations of 0.99 for rating distributions and 0.949 for blocking distributions; these and the model distribution comparisons are accurately summarized (PDF pp.7-8).

The replication permits one chat at a time for seekers and counselors, while the live platform permits counselors multiple simultaneous chats; the authors cite this as a likely reason simulated matching is lower (78.35% vs 83.27%) (PDF p.8).

Topic-based recommendation in the Where Does it Apply / What Can it Answer summary and outcome measures remain appropriately framed as simulation results. Footnotes r3-r6 now point to specific source procedures/pages.
notes.limits: No material predictor, validation, status-quo, recommendation randomization, or replication-limit issue remains in the corrected note.
